prompt.context: Our client is an online dating startup named Grad-U-Date, which specializes in matching graduate students with other graduate students. Grad-U-Date has finished building their app and are now looking for your assistance in deciding on a monetization strategy.
prompt.question: What is Grad-U-Date's best method of monetization? How profitable will the company be?

clarifying_info.q: What is the gender ratio of users?
clarifying_info.a: The gender ratio of users will be 50/50.

clarifying_info.q: Which graduate students are considered professional students?
clarifying_info.a: MBA, law, and medical students are considered professional students.

clarifying_info.q: Has the app already been built? Should we factor in development costs?
clarifying_info.a: The app has already been built and is considered a sunk cost.

clarifying_info.q: In which geographies will Grad-U-Date operate?
clarifying_info.a: Grad-U-Date will only operate within the United States.

clarifying_info.q: What does the competitive landscape look like?
clarifying_info.a: There are 4 major competitors and hundreds of small competitors.

clarifying_info.q: Are there other online dating services focused on graduate students?
clarifying_info.a: There are currently no other online dating services that focus only on graduate students.

clarifying_info.q: Can Grad-U-Date use multiple revenue models simultaneously?
clarifying_info.a: Only one revenue model can be used.

exhibits.title: Student Enrolment Information
exhibits.shows: A bar chart showing new graduate students per university per year by program type, along with the number of years required for each degree. Note: There are currently 1,000 universities in the United States.

exhibits.title: Product Usage and Revenue Model Parameters
exhibits.shows: A bar chart showing forecasted percentage of graduate students using Grad-U-Date under each revenue model (Monthly Fee: 5%, Premium Account: 30%, Advertising: 40%), plus descriptions of each model's pricing.

data.Advertising Model: Non-professional students bring in $0.75 per month; professional students bring in $1.25 per month in ad revenue
data.Premium Account Model: Premium accounts cost $5 per month; 40% of men and 20% of women purchase premium accounts

exhibits.title: Online Dating Market Trends
exhibits.shows: A dual-axis line chart showing trends from 2008 to 2014 in the percentage of online dating users paying a monthly fee and the average monthly fee amount in dollars.

data.description: From 2008 to 2014, both the percentage of users paying monthly fees and the average monthly fee have been declining, with a sharp drop starting around 2013.

framework: Understand the market: estimate total addressable market of graduate students in the US
Assess competitive landscape: major vs. small competitors, existing gaps (no grad-student-only competitor)
Identify monetization options: monthly fee, advertising, premium account, and others (pay-per-message, micro-transactions, profile consulting)
Evaluate each model: forecast users, revenue, and profit under each option
Recommend the highest-profit model; validate against market trends

questions.prompt: What types of monetization models could Grad-U-Date use, and what are the advantages and disadvantages of each?
questions.guidance: Candidate should brainstorm at least 3 models (strong candidates brainstorm 5+). Models include: (1) Monthly Fee — simple, predictable revenue, but limits user base and segment is shrinking; (2) Advertising — large user base, lower revenue per user, revenue depends on user engagement; (3) Premium Account (freemium) — broad free base drives network effects, revenue from subset of engaged users; (4) Profile Consulting Services — high value per user, limited scale; (5) Micro-Transactions (e.g., pay per message, pay for profile bump) — flexible monetization but unpredictable. Candidate should remain structured with pros and cons.

questions.prompt: Grad-U-Date is considering limiting the site to only MBA students. What issues might there be with an MBA-only dating website?
questions.guidance: Strong answers cover: (1) Gender skew — more men than women at most MBA programs; (2) Unnecessary market limitation — shrinks addressable user base significantly; (3) MBA students tend to be older and more likely to already be married or in committed relationships.

questions.prompt: What is the potential market size for Grad-U-Date? [Use Exhibit 1]
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate total enrolled graduate students in the US using new students per year multiplied by years for each degree, then sum across program types and multiply by number of universities.

math.setup: Total enrolled = (new students per year per program × years for degree) × 1,000 universities. Sum across all program types.

questions.prompt: Calculate the profit of each revenue model. Fixed costs are $10,000,000 per year and variable operating cost is $1 per member per year. Which revenue model would you recommend? [Use Exhibit 2]
questions.guidance: Candidate should compute customers, revenue, and profit for all three models, then compare. Monthly Fee yields the highest profit and should be the initial recommendation.

math.setup: Profit = Revenue − Fixed Costs − (Variable Cost × Number of Users). Market size = 6,000,000.
math.answer: Monthly Fee: $25,700,000 profit | Premium Account: $20,600,000 profit | Advertising: $16,400,000 profit. Initial recommendation: Monthly Fee.

questions.prompt: Does the market trend information change your recommendation for which revenue model? [Use Exhibit 3]
questions.guidance: Candidate should switch recommendation from Monthly Fee to Premium Account. The exhibit shows that the percentage of users paying monthly fees and the average monthly fee have both been declining sharply since 2008, with acceleration around 2013. The Monthly Fee segment is shrinking rapidly, making long-term profitability uncertain. Premium Account is a more defensible choice.

questions.prompt: Why do you think that the percentage of users paying monthly fees dropped so quickly starting in 2013?
questions.guidance: Candidates should identify: (1) Increased competition in the online dating market; (2) Quality free dating apps were released that are more convenient; (3) Specifically, the Tinder app launched in late 2012, introducing a dominant free swipe-based model that changed user expectations.

questions.prompt: Given your recommended revenue model (Premium Account), what other strategies can Grad-U-Date use to increase profit?
questions.guidance: Strong candidates structure answers into Reduce Costs vs. Increase Revenue buckets. Reduce Costs: outsource servers, provide only email support (no phone). Increase Revenue: create an app to attract more customers, offer profile consulting services, profile photo editing, deals with popular date locations, expand to recent graduate school alumni, add micro-transactions (e.g., paying to boost profile traffic).

brainstorming.prompt: What types of monetization models could Grad-U-Date use, and what are the advantages and disadvantages of each?

categories.name: Subscription / Access Fees
ideas: Monthly membership fee ($10/month) — predictable revenue but limits user base and segment is declining
Annual subscription — lower churn, but upfront commitment barrier

categories.name: Freemium / Premium Accounts
ideas: Free basic account with paid premium tier ($5/month) — broad user base with monetization of engaged subset
40% of men and 20% of women purchase premium accounts

categories.name: Advertising
ideas: In-app display advertising — larger user base, revenue scales with engagement
Professional students yield higher ad revenue ($1.25/month) vs. non-professional ($0.75/month)

categories.name: Value-Added / Transactional Services
ideas: Profile consulting services — high value per transaction, limited scale
Pay per message — pay only when actively using
Pay for profile traffic bump / micro-transactions — incremental revenue from engaged users

categories.name: Partnerships
ideas: Deals with popular date locations (restaurants, cinemas)
Partnerships with florists or gift services

recommendation: Grad-U-Date should adopt the Premium Account revenue model
The Monthly Fee model should not be selected: the monthly-fee segment is rapidly disappearing (sharp decline in user share and average fee since 2008) and it limits the platform user base
The Premium Account model is expected to generate $20,600,000 in annual profit
risks: Premium account adoption could be seeing a similar decline in share as the monthly fee model
A smaller percentage of users than forecast may purchase premium accounts
The advertising-supported model could be growing faster than premium account, making it more attractive over time
Graduate students may not be able to afford premium accounts
Number of people attending graduate school could decrease, shrinking the total addressable market
Graduate students may not want to limit their dating pool to other grad students only
next_steps: Investigate market trends for advertising and premium account revenue models to validate long-run attractiveness
Expand into new markets such as undergraduates or international universities
Offer additional services: profile consulting and date-location deals
Add micro-transactions such as boosting profile traffic
Explore integrating social media to increase user acquisition
Evaluate whether premium account and advertising models could be combined
